$why: Moved out of code-review-cycle.sh on 2026-08-15 (18 of 20).
The reviewer PROFILE arrives as a value: it is the project-authority half of what this
agent is told, and it belongs to profiles.json rather than to this template.

2026-08-19: issues carried no evidence, and code-review-json.py accepted any object with a verdict. The reviewer twice asserted the Contentstack SDK would not recognise `management_token`; the installed index.d.ts declares exactly that and never mentions preview_token. An earlier draw of the same seam checked the types unprompted and got it right — correctness was luck. Unevidenced issues are now discarded, so the prompt has to ask for evidence.
body:
__REVIEW_PROFILE__

---
REVIEW TASK (Iteration __ITERATION__): Story __STORY_ID__ — __STORY_TITLE__
AGENT: __STORY_AGENT__

DESCRIPTION: __STORY_DESCRIPTION__

RELEVANT FILES: __STORY_FILES__

GIT DIFF:
```diff
__STORY_DIFF__
```
__PRIOR_CONTEXT__
PROJECT ROOT: __PROJECT_ROOT__

Review the implementation against each acceptance criterion.
Check: TypeScript strict compliance, test coverage, error handling, security.

Respond with ONLY a JSON object:
{"verdict":"approved","issues":[],"summary":"..."}
  OR
{"verdict":"changes_requested","issues":[{"severity":"blocker|major|minor","file":"...","line":0,"description":"...","evidence":"<path>:<line> you read, or the command you ran and its result","suggestedFix":"..."}],"summary":"..."}

Every issue MUST carry an `evidence` field: the exact thing you READ that establishes it — `<path>:<line>` you opened, or the command you ran and what it returned. Not a restatement of the claim, not a plan reference: what you looked at. An issue without evidence is DISCARDED before it reaches anyone, so an unsupported finding is worse than no finding — it costs you the issue. If a claim is about a library's API, the evidence is that library's installed types or source in this repository, and the installed contract beats the plan.
description: Review an implementation and return a verdict with issues.
$mayBeEmpty: __PRIOR_CONTEXT__ carries the PREVIOUS iteration's findings, and iteration 1 has no previous iteration — code-review-cycle.sh sets it only `when iteration > 1`. Without this declaration the library refused every render on a first review, so the seam could not perform an initial review at all: it printed 'cannot render its prompt — refusing to run with no instructions' and the caller saw a review that never happened. Absent is a REAL state here, which is exactly what mayBeEmpty is for.
